title: Model 2 R18 neural correction: clean re-evaluation matches a constant-shift control
scope: Model 2 R18 seed 11 learned correction versus physics and a constant-vector control on 19 held-out Sentinel-2 pairs, plus a footprint-aware pair benchmark.
summary: On 19 held-out pairs, centroid error was 43.5 km for wind-only physics, 47.9 km for current-coupled physics, 28.8 km for R18 seed 11 and 25.9 km for the mean of 20 seeds. Wind-only physics plus one constant 37.8 km eastward shift scored 23.6 km, so the network adds nothing beyond a constant shift. This challenges the earlier R18 result, but the sample is small and the project documents do not yet agree on R18 status. In a footprint-corrected benchmark (42 pairs scored by every arm, 72 h) no arm was distinguishable from persistence.

limitations: The source report is an untracked working-tree file; it is identified by SHA-256 only and has no source commit.
Pair offsets track the differing image footprints of the two scenes: pooled correlation 0.77 between footprint offset and forecast residual, so cross-orbit pairs conflate footprint with transport.
The planned common-footprint rescoring failed (timeout, then a crash) and its pre-registered criterion was never evaluated.
The pair benchmark is underpowered: only about 20% of predicted mass lands in the observed strip.
The only consistent signal is that east bias falls as windage rises toward 2 to 3 percent.
Small sample (19 pairs) on exposed data; the project documents do not yet agree on R18 status, so earlier R18 records are kept as published.

evidence.summary: Clean R18 re-evaluation, footprint analysis and pair benchmark in the final delivery report v8, sections 1 to 3.
